title: Silent Night
description: Silent Night in Tonic Solfa (doh is Bb): the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all three verses and a piano to sing along with.
about: Joseph Mohr, a young priest in Austria, wrote the German words; Franz Xaver Gruber, the local schoolmaster and organist, set them to music, and the carol was first sung at Christmas 1818 in Oberndorf. The English words most churches sing are John Freeman Young's translation of three of Mohr's verses.
The tune is in 6/8: count two beats in a bar, each beat split into three. In the solfa grid every cell is half a crotchet, so a bar has six cells.
underlay: Si-lent night,_ ho-ly night,_ All is calm, all is bright, Round yon vir-gin moth-er and child._ Ho-ly in-fant so ten-der and mild, Sleep in heav-en-ly peace,_ Sleep in heav-en-ly peace._

lines: All is calm, all is bright
Round yon Virgin Mother and Child.
Holy Infant, so tender and mild,
Son of God, love’s pure light;
Radiant beams from Thy holy face
With the dawn of redeeming grace,
